So, starting from what you have, poking around with `readelf` and `LD_DEBUG=bindings`, we get:

```

ninja: Entering directory `/home/andrew/src/openbmc.org/openbmc/libpldm/origin/build.trixie'
[28/28] Linking target tests/oem_ibm_fileio
[I] 0 andrew@heihei ~/s/o/o/l/origin ((bb22eb16))> readelf -Ws /home/andrew/src/openbmc.org/openbmc/libpldm/origin/build.trixie/src/libpldm.so.0 | grep libpldm_
  1075: 000000000000f600    96 FUNC    LOCAL  DEFAULT   12 libpldm_clock_gettimeval
  1091: 000000000000f570   135 FUNC    LOCAL  DEFAULT   12 libpldm_timeval_is_valid
  1101: 000000000000f540    46 FUNC    LOCAL  DEFAULT   12 libpldm_timeval_to_msec
[I] 0 andrew@heihei ~/s/o/o/l/origin ((bb22eb16))> readelf -Ws build.trixie/tests/transport_send_recv_timeout | grep libpldm
  7192: 0000000000028e40    13 FUNC    WEAK   DEFAULT   14 _Z24libpldm_clock_gettimevalP7timeval
[I] 0 andrew@heihei ~/s/o/o/l/origin ((bb22eb16))> LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/andrew/src/openbmc.org/openbmc/libpldm/origin/build.trixie/src LD_DEBUG=bindings /home/andrew/src/openbmc.org/openbmc/libpldm/origin/build.trixie/tests/transport_send_recv_timeout 2>&1 | grep libpldm_clock_gettimeval
```

Things to notice here are:

1. The symbol in `transport_send_recv_timeout` has had C++ name mangling applied (`_Z24libpldm_clock_gettimevalP7timeval`) while the symbol in `libpldm.so.0` has not (`libpldm_clock_gettimeval`)
2. That `libpldm_clock_gettimeval` in `libpldm.so.0` is marked `LOCAL` while the intended symbol in `transport_send_recv_timeout` is marked `WEAK`.

Regarding 2, it should be the case that the symbol in `libpldm.so.0` is marked `WEAK` and the one in `transport_send_recv_timeout` is marked `FUNC` (and neither are marked `LOCAL`).

Hi Amithash. I have a bit of a strong preference against naming things 'utils' because the only thing that happens from that point is they start collecting cruft. See the current `utils.[ch]` contents for an example.

I thought about the problem a bit and settled on the observation that we're calling out to the environment for some external information, and as such it might be best if we recognise that in the source structure. The concept is that any hooks to e.g. libc or other dependencies can be put in their respective header under `src/environ/`.

Anyway, with that sorted, I have a couple of further requests inline.

A couple of things:

Can you please replace the open-coded `__attribute__((weak))` here with `LIBPLDM_CC_WEAK`, and define `LIBPLDM_CC_WEAK` in `src/compiler.h`?

I also prefer that things in `src/environ/` wrap e.g. the libc APIs directly. So rather than `libpldm_clock_gettimeval()` here, we instead have `libpldm_clock_gettime()`, whose implementation is only a call to `clock_gettime()`. The conversion logic to `struct timeval` continues to live in `src/transport/transport.c`.
Done!
I think I addressed all the comments. Moved the compiler bits into its own gerrit.
